description: Exploration is about real expeditions: what exploration is, its history and fields, living explorers, and planning, preparing for and carrying out an expedition of your own, then reporting what you learned.

safety.note: Expeditions need permission, an approved plan and qualified adult supervision.

versions.label: Checked against official scouting.org excerpts (partial verification)

provenance.notes: Requirement numbering and topics were checked against excerpts of official Scouting America pages (scouting.org) returned by a search index on 2026-10-24. The pages themselves could not be opened from the build environment, so wording was not compared word for word and some sub-items may be summarized from partial excerpts. Summaries are ScoutPath's own words. Excerpts were jumbled for requirements 3–5, which are not outlined yet. The 2026 update revised requirements 8 and 9.

references.label: Official merit badge page (scouting.org Merit Badge Hub)

requirements.title: What exploration is
requirements.summary: How exploration differs from adventure travel, and how it works in settings from oceans to space to labs.

requirements.title: History of exploration
requirements.summary: The history of exploration and one field of study that shows its importance.

requirements.title: Planning an expedition
requirements.summary: Objectives, budget, equipment, communications, transportation, safety, first aid and team selection.

requirements.title: Preparing for an expedition
requirements.summary: Working with a qualified leader, listing gear and deciding who goes.

requirements.title: An expedition
requirements.summary: Carrying out a supervised expedition to a new area, practicing outdoor ethics, and writing a report.

requirements.title: Careers
requirements.summary: Researching a career related to exploration.
